definition: Deep Instinct is a cybersecurity company that applies deep learning to cybersecurity.
details: The company implements artificial intelligence to the task of preventing and detecting malware. The company was the recipient of the Technology Pioneer by The World Economic Forum in 2017. Lane Bess has been CEO of the company since 2022.

explainer.lead: Deep Instinct is a company working on a focused use of artificial intelligence: stopping malicious software and detecting it. Its work puts deep learning directly in the service of cybersecurity.

tiers.eli5: Deep Instinct works like a security guard that has studied many examples of trouble. It uses deep learning to help spot harmful software and stop it before it can do damage.
tiers.practitioner: For an engineer, Deep Instinct belongs in a cybersecurity evaluation focused on malware prevention and detection. It is a company applying deep learning, not a general-purpose neural-network framework, and its internal architecture or configuration should not be assumed from the company-level description.
tiers.paperLevel: Deep Instinct = a cybersecurity company applying deep learning to malware prevention and detection. No model architecture, training objective, dataset, or quantitative evaluation is specified, so its description supports an application-level characterization rather than a formal algorithmic one.

explainer.example: A company encounters a suspicious program on one of its computers. Deep Instinct's deep-learning-based approach is intended to identify the program as malware and help prevent it from causing harm.
